ai.description: This small frog reaches 25–30 mm. It is distinctively bright red to orange with a dark, inverted V-shaped mark on the back and a cream-colored belly. It lacks webbing between the toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes resplendens* is uniquely distinguished by the vivid, bright orange-red coloration on its dorsal surface, which contrasts sharply with its dark, mottled flanks.
ai.habitat: The Resplendent Bush Frog inhabits high-altitude shola grasslands and stunted evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 2,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Resplendent Bush Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden within high-altitude shola grasslands and forest canopy during the day to avoid predators and desiccation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes resplendens* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They lay small clutches of terrestrial eggs during the monsoon season (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: The Resplendent Bush Frog is endemic to the high-altitude shola forests of the Anamudi peak in the Western Ghats, Kerala, at elevations above 2,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Resplendent Bush Frog emits a high-pitched, insect-like series of short, metallic chirps, typically heard from vegetation within high-altitude shola grasslands.
